newsitem.title: USA: Clinton adds 10 cities to gun tracking program.
newsitem.headline: Clinton adds 10 cities to gun tracking program.

text.p: President Clinton announced plans on Saturday to add 10 more cities to a programme for tracking the sale of illegal guns to young people through a national computer system.
He said the year-old programme had proved successful in the 17 cities -- tracking 37,000 guns used in crimes, many of which were traced back to networks of gun traffickers and corrupt gun dealers.
"Make no mistake -- gun traffickers are funnelling guns to lawless youth. We know how they operate and we intend to shut them down," Clinton said in his weekly radio address.

Under the initiative introduced by the president during the 1996 election campaign, police chiefs and prosecutors from 17 cities pledged to provide information on every gun they seized from a juvenile during a crime.

The data was fed into a computer system run by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms (ATF). The objective of the $2 million-a-year programme was to trace each gun back to its seller in an attempt to find out who was selling guns to juveniles and prosecute them.
Results released Saturday by the Treasury Department, which oversees the ATF, showed that almost half of all guns used in crimes came from young people 24 and under.
Their weapon of choice was the semiautomatic pistol, comprising 60 percent of the crime guns recovered.
"One crucial fact is now clear -- that guns are finding their way quickly from legitimate retail stores to black markets through a network of gun traffickers and corrupt gun dealers," Clinton said.
He praised the ATF and others who worked on the youth gun-tracing initiative and said it had been so effective that it would be expanded to 10 more cities, including Los Angeles and Philadelphia.

"Our most recent figures even show a slight decline in juvenile crime, but we all know that juvenile crime and violence are still significant problems ... children are still killing children for shoes, for jackets, for turf," he said.
Clinton said that over past decades, the number of gun murders by juveniles had skyrocketed by 300 percent and that such a situation was "simply unacceptable."
But he noted that some cities had begun to break the trend, in particular Boston, where not a single juvenile murder had been committed with a gun in two years.
"A year ago, I looked at Boston's approach and it was clear that tracing guns seized from young criminals was a key to the city's success," Clinton said.
The new cities participating in the programme included: Chicago, Detroit, Philadelphia, Los Angeles, Gary, Ind., Miami, Minneapolis, Houston, Cinncinati and Tuscon, Ariz., the White House said.
Clinton also urged Congress to build on the progress made through the ATF programme by passing "a smart, tough" juvenile justice bill.

He also said he was disappointed that a Senate committee last week voted against ordering federal firearms dealers to provide child-safety locks on weapons and urged local officials to voluntarily perform background checks on gun-buying adults after a Supreme Court ruling struck down a provision of the law requiring them to do so.
In the Republican response, Representative Jennifer Dunn of Washington state praised tax proposals approved by the House as giving "women across America ... a tax cut."
"Helping American families, and especially America's women is all part of the Republican agenda," she said.
House and Senate negotiators currently are trying to work out differences in their respective tax legislation so that a final tax cut bill can go before Congress for a vote.
